name: Shining Strand
summary: Along eastern Silverpine, Shining Strand follows Lordamere Lake south from the Ruins of Lordaeron toward Alterac's rugged foothills. Vile Fin murlocs hold settlements in its shallows, making the shore dangerous for unseasoned travelers.

sections.title: A Contested Coastline
sections.body: Shining Strand follows Silverpine Forest's eastern edge beside the misty waters of Lordamere Lake. Several aggressive Vile Fin murloc settlements line the shallows, threatening anyone who travels the lake road. Feral worgen roam the deep woods behind the shore.

sections.title: Alchemical Harvest
sections.body: Royal Apothecary Society attention reached Shining Strand and its neighboring waters. The late Apothecary Berard recorded unusual hardened tumors harvested from local Vile Fin murlocs. He theorized their corrupted anatomy could make the tumors a valuable catalyst for concocting a new plague for Sylvanas Windrunner's fledgling nation.

faq.q: Where is the Shining Strand located?
faq.answer: Shining Strand runs along Silverpine Forest's eastern shore, beside Lordamere Lake. It stretches south from the Ruins of Lordaeron to the rugged hills separating Silverpine from the Alterac Mountains.

faq.q: What threats are found along the Shining Strand?
faq.answer: Vile Fin murlocs hold several settlements along the shore and attack unwary travelers. Feral worgen prowl the Silverpine woods beyond the strand.

faq.q: Why is the Royal Apothecary Society interested in this area?
faq.answer: The Royal Apothecary Society is interested because the late Apothecary Berard documented hardened tumors in local Vile Fin murlocs, with unique physiological traits. He theorized the growths could serve as a catalyst for concocting a new plague.
The Vile Fin are the murloc tribe whose settlements line Shining Strand, making the lakeshore dangerous for unseasoned travelers.

angles.text: The Royal Apothecary Society studies the Vile Fin murlocs of Shining Strand in hopes of concocting a new plague.
Lordamere Lake's shore links Silverpine's northern approaches with passages toward the Alterac Mountains, though the strand is perilous.
